title: EverQuest
shortDescription: Sony Online Entertainment and Brad McQuaid's monumental 3D MMORPG that defined the modern online multiplayer role-playing genre.
historicalSignificance: The foundational 3D MMORPG that popularized subscription-based online virtual worlds in the West, peaking at over 500,000 active concurrent players and creating the blueprint directly adopted by World of Warcraft.

editorialContent.overview: Set in the high-fantasy world of Norrath, EverQuest invited thousands of players to step inside a fully 3D persistent online universe, choose from 14 distinct fantasy races and classes, and forge lifelong guilds.
editorialContent.gameplay: Strictly group-oriented cooperative raiding: tank-healer-DPS trinity combat, deadly corpse runs upon death, complex spell memorization, and epic multi-hour dragon raids in dungeons like Plane of Fear.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Pioneered large-scale 3D client-server network architecture capable of synchronizing thousands of simultaneous players across continuous seamless zone servers over dial-up modems.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Became a worldwide cultural phenomenon dubbed 'EverCrack' due to its legendary social bonding, inspiring sociologists and economists to study virtual economies and guild governance.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on original CD-ROMs and actively running on persistent servers for over 25 consecutive years.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over 500,000 active monthly subscribers (genre record in 2001)
awards: Inducted into World Video Game Hall of Fame Nominee
